1795.unvetted: TNA Discovery (API, read 6 Nov 2026) now settles part of the old note: SP 89/12/73 (f.123, 29 Jul/3 Aug 1672, Parry to Arlington) carries the catalogue note 'Deciphered copy. See f.124', and SP 89/12/74 (f.124) is 'Original of f.123' with note 'Partly in cipher'. So this lead's own shelfmark is the contemporary decipherment, and the ciphertext is f.124 (a separate document, not this lead). Verdict would be read/partly_read (or a reframe onto f.124), but no leaf has been seen: not digitised on Discovery, State Papers Online is Gale (subscription), no calendar covers SP 89 Portugal 1672. Three web searches this pass (Parry/Arlington/de Mello 1672 deciphered; Parry/Ferreira Rebello/Brazil Company; Tomokiyo/cryptiana/SP 106 Parry) found only the two TNA records, no edition and no cryptiana page. Unblock: a Kew or SPO view of ff.123-124 to confirm the decipher sits with the cipher, then close as read.

1802.unvetted: Re-tried this pass: Discovery API record C7306165 for SP 84/161/83 (f.216, undated, 1656 volume) says only 'Letter in cipher or shorthand, mentioning Peter Refin of Middelburg'; no author, language or content summary, and the neighbouring folios (f.163 Admiralty report, f.167 Whittell to Dorislaus, f.231 Aizema extracts) give no context. Searches for 'Peter/Pieter Refin' Middelburg 1656, for SP 84/161 with cipher/shorthand, and for Thurloe State Papers vol. 5 Middelburg/Refin found no hit on this letter or person (Thurloe papers are SP 18/Rawlinson, not SP 84, and no calendar covers SP 84/161). The cataloguer's own 'cipher or shorthand' leaves open that it is shorthand (not a cipher), so ciphertext is not shown. Unblock: a Kew or SPO leaf view to tell cipher from shorthand.

1804.unvetted: Re-tried this pass: Discovery API record C10687619 for SP 94/8/197 reads only 'Folio 197: Cipher Marseilles. In Italian', language Italian, undated; neighbours are f.195-196 (Spanish condemnations of royal finance officers, dated 1563 in the catalogue) and f.198-199 (Spanish copy of instructions for Henry Pranell), so the date, the writer and even the volume context are uncertain. 'Cipher Marseilles' reads like the title of a key or nomenclator, not a ciphertext, and nothing in the description shows ciphertext survives. known.py on SP 94/8 and 'Cipher Marseilles' found nothing, and web searches for SP 94/8 Marseilles Italian cipher and for the Pranell instructions turned up no edition or calendar. Unblock: a Kew or SPO view of f.197 to see whether it is a letter or a key.

1136.unvetted: Aggregate: one record for 63 cipher-marked items across PRO 30/11/3-6, 68-69, 81-87 with no single document named, so it stays unvetted by the third-pass rule. This pass found that decipherment is on record for part of it: Saberton, 'Decoding British ciphers used in the South, 1780-81' (allthingsliberty.com, 2019) says he decoded the Rawdon-to-Watson cipher letter (printed deciphered in Gibbes, Documentary History of the American Revolution 3: 31-2) and cites his Cornwallis Papers (CP 4: 47-9, 4: 50, 5: 139, 2: 129) for Common- and Alternative-cipher letters; Ross 1859 prints a few. So many of the 63 are likely partly_read, and which are not cannot be told without Saberton's six volumes, which are not online (searches for Saberton Cornwallis Papers cipher decoded, JAR cipher articles and Clinton/Cornwallis Yorktown code found no per-item concordance). Unblock: Saberton's CP index per shelfmark, then split into per-letter leads.

1137.unvetted: Aggregate: series-level record for 25 items in PRO 30/55 (Carleton Papers), so no single document; it stays unvetted. This pass read the Discovery records (API, 6 Nov 2026): 55/16/146 and /147 are Haldimand's proposed cypher of 26 May 1779 (a key, no ciphertext), 55/19/98 is 'Clinton to Haldimand. Letter in cypher' (22 Oct 1779, no content summary, a candidate single lead), and 55/24/76 is an undated cypher letter whose description gives the content (a French fleet bound for Canada, found by comparison with a British Museum copy), i.e. a decipherment is on record there. Not digitised. Searches (Clinton/Haldimand cypher 1779 PRO 30/55 deciphered; Report on Canadian Archives; Saberton) found no per-item decipherment or edition. Unblock: split by item, starting with 55/19/98, and check the Haldimand Papers (BL Add MS 21,000 series, Report on Canadian Archives 1886-89) for printed plaintexts.

1146.unvetted: Aggregate: seven unrelated items from different series and decades (SP 81/44/225, 81/46/273, 84/130/27, 77/28/643, 81/37/284, 81/38/250, 77/6/229), none digitised, so no single document; it stays unvetted. Discovery API (6 Nov 2026) confirms the descriptions: 81/44/225 Roe July 1638 'postscript in cipher', 81/46/273 'Portion in cipher concerning Prince Palatine and France', 84/130/27 c.Nov 1625 'Portion in cipher concerning Mansfelt', 77/28/643 'Gerbier - cipher letter on Taylor's accusations', 81/37/284 'Duplicate of paper sent by Mr. Stanning in cipher', 81/38/250 Vane extracts in cipher, 77/6/229 Kendall to Cecil 1600 'in cipher'. Akkerman's edition of Elizabeth Stuart's correspondence (OUP 2011-15, cipher keys in an appendix) is not online and none of the searches (Akkerman Roe/Gerbier/Kendall; Roe 1638 postscript SP 81/44; known.py on each shelfmark, no hits) says whether these State Papers items are printed deciphered. Unblock: Akkerman vol. 2 index/appendix, then one lead per item (77/6/229 Kendall to Cecil is the cleanest).

1151.unvetted: Aggregate: series-level (SP 91/5, about 50 folios, Whitworth Moscow 1707-08) naming no single undeciphered folio, and it overlaps catalogue entries already held (863 for Whitworth's Russia despatches, and the entry for SP 91/6 plus SP 91/5/298), so it stays unvetted. This pass: Discovery search (6 Nov 2026) lists 48 Whitworth items 1707-08 in SP 91/5 with no per-item cipher flag in the description text; the Sbornik of the Russian Historical Society vol. 50 (1708-11) prints Whitworth's despatches with Russian translation and an earlier volume covers 1704-08 (volume number unconfirmed, not online in text), so printed versions may carry decipherments. Searches (Whitworth Moscow Sbornik cipher; Whitworth Harley/Boyle cipher; known.py SP 91/5 and Whitworth) found only the catalogue entries. Unblock: open the Sbornik volumes and split off any folio left undeciphered that is not already in 863 or the SP 91/6 entry.
